rationale: packages/babel-types/test/asserts.js imports the whole @babel/types namespace as t, iterates Object.keys(t), and for every key starting with 'assert' (except assertNode) calls t[k](...), which invokes assertTupleTypeAnnotation. That is a non-literal computed-key call on an object holding the function, exactly the obj[name]() pattern dynamic-property-keyed-callback describes. fp-novel is defensible because the 'object' is a module namespace imported via ../lib/index.js rather than a literal map.
prior_verdicts_assessment: The tp verdict is wrong: it grepped for the literal name and missed the Object.keys(t) loop in the babel-types asserts test that calls every exported assert function.
